# UploadClientMimeTrusted

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" />

Group: [Security](/rules/#security)

Detect acceptance of an upload based solely on $_FILES entry type compared to an allowed MIME string without server-side content inspection.

## Example

```php{2,5}
<?php
if ($_FILES['file']['type'] === 'image/png') { move_uploaded_file($_FILES['file']['tmp_name'], '/srv/uploads/image.png'); }
function storeAvatar() {
    if (!in_array($_FILES['avatar']['type'], ['image/png', 'image/jpeg'], true)) { return; }
    move_uploaded_file($_FILES['avatar']['tmp_name'], '/srv/avatars/new');
}
function storeScan() {
    if ($_FILES['scan']['type'] !== 'image/png') { return; }
    if (getimagesize($_FILES['scan']['tmp_name']) === false) { return; } // content inspected: no report
    move_uploaded_file($_FILES['scan']['tmp_name'], '/srv/scans/new');
}
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Inspect uploaded content instead of trusting its client MIME label.</li>
<li>line 5: Inspect uploaded content instead of trusting its client MIME label.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- Report a builtin `move_uploaded_file()` call whose source is `$_FILES[key]['tmp_name']` (literal key) when the call is reached only if the client-supplied `$_FILES[key]['type']` of the same entry matched an allowed MIME string, and no server-side content inspection of that temporary file is found (E1).
- A client type test is `$_FILES[key]['type']` (a literal key, or a local holding one that stays unchanged, as does every `$_FILES` element, up to the call) compared (`==`, `===`, `!=`, `!==`, either operand order) with a string literal, or a builtin `in_array()` call (positional or named arguments) whose needle is that entry type and whose haystack is a non-empty literal array of string literals, searched strictly or, when no value reads as a number, loosely.
- The call is reached only if the type matched: the conditions guarding it limit the entry type to string literals that all contain `/`. Tests combine through `!`, parentheses, `&&`/`and` and `||`/`or` (each side of a disjunction must limit it), and guard the call from the branch of an `if`/`elseif`/`else` chain, a ternary or `match (true)` arm, the right operand of `&&`/`||`, or code after an `if` whose branch for another type always leaves (return, throw, exit, break, continue), with or without other arms.
- A call of the project between the test and the call, which may write `$_FILES`, a jump label between them, a write to the entry, or a test of another entry proves nothing.
- Resolve builtin calls and named arguments before checking the contract. Project-local callees are considered only when their bodies or immutable summaries establish the required facts. The default is enabled, with positive proof required.
- For flow-dependent conditions, require a reachable source-to-use path with no intervening invalidation. Unknown calls, ambiguous aliases, recursion or analysis-budget exhaustion cannot establish definite facts.

## Exceptions (no report)

- E1. Server-side content inspection: anywhere earlier in the same function (or script) the same temporary file, written as `$_FILES[key]['tmp_name']` or as a local variable assigned from it, is an argument of builtin `finfo_file()`, `mime_content_type()`, `getimagesize()`, `exif_imagetype()`, an `imagecreatefrom*()` decoder, or a method call named `file` (`finfo::file()`; the receiver type need not be proven). The inspection does not have to dominate the move: an acceptance path that may depend on stored bytes is not provably label-only.
- Client MIME used only for display, logging or choosing a name; a test that rejects the allowed type; a guard that does not leave; a `||` alternative in an accepting branch or a `&&` in a guard (the test is then not required); a different `$_FILES` entry; and upload-error or size checks alone are not client type tests.
- Unresolved targets, incomplete required facts, suppressed findings and PHP versions lacking the referenced API or language feature produce no report. User declarations shadowing builtin names are not builtin contracts.

## Fix

No automatic fix: content types, file size limits and image decoding policy must be selected by the application.

## PHP versions

Apply only on PHP versions supporting the referenced APIs and syntax (within PHP 5.3–8.5). Builtin behavior and argument contracts follow the configured PHP version. Extension-specific calls require resolved extension API symbols; do not treat same-named application functions as extension calls.

## Options

None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "UploadClientMimeTrusted": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore UploadClientMimeTrusted
```
